prerequisites: Competences associated with Industrial Automation course (recommended)

learning_outcomes.text: Introduce the student to the fundamental concepts of manipulation and mobile robotics, as well as the description of their peripherals, so that they are able to analyze, design, program, and use these types of systems and adapt to their evolution.
Describe the techniques used in the trajectory control that a robotic manipulator must follow when performing a task.
Describe the automatic control techniques used for the control of a robotic manipulator's actuators.
Describe the teaching methods for robotic manipulators, either through direct learning or through robot programming languages: textual, task-level, etc.
Introduce the criteria, norms, and techniques necessary for the design and implementation of robotic cells for problem-solving.
The student will understand the applications of robots and their scope in different areas of society.

The student will understand the fundamentals of manipulation robotics, being able to calculate the direct and inverse kinematic and dynamic model, considering each robot segment as a rigid body. Additionally, they will know how to calculate the controllers associated with each of its joints to follow a desired trajectory in space.

The student will understand the fundamentals of mobile robotics and autonomous vehicles, will know how to calculate their direct kinematic model, as well as various algorithms for tracing and calculating trajectories and paths in known and unknown environments.
Ability in the use of ICT
Knowledge of principles and applications of robotic systems

syllabus_topics: Modeling and control of industrial robots
Basic programming of a robotic manipulator and integration of the robot in the manufacturing process
Layout of elements of a robotic system on the plant floor with RobotStudio
Programming of a robotic cell with RobotStudio
teaching_methods: Assimilation of knowledge from theoretical classes
Solving exercises proposed in lectures/participative classes
Solving practical cases proposed in laboratory practices
Use of interactive material hosted on the Mechanical Engineering Area server
assessment_rules: For the ordinary call, the final grade is calculated as (0.25*Problems + 0.3*Practice Report and Interview + 0.4*Exam + 0.05*Participation) * AI_Usage_Factor. A minimum score of 5 points is required in Problems, Practices, and Exam to pass. The 'Ability in the use of ICTs' competence must be passed (evaluated via lab practices and exercises) with at least 'Pass' for the course to be approved. Lab practices require a minimum of 5 points each and an oral interview. AI usage must be declared and adhere to good practices, otherwise, the AI_Usage_Factor is 0. For the extraordinary call and single assessment, the grading formula and minimum scores are similar, with provisions for resubmitting practices or alternative practices for those unable to attend, and personal interviews for participation if there was no prior contact.
